newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper seen ripe for profit-taking - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper seen ripe for profit-taking - trade.

text.p: Far East metal dealers said the three-month copper contract on the London Metal Exchange (LME) is ripe for some profit-taking later on Wednesday after a modest rally took the red metal above the US$2,280 a tonne level.
"I hope to see some profit-taking when it hits $2,285," a dealer for a European metal trading firm said. "It will probably be sold down again at that level."
The rest of the base metal complex will probably be range-bound trade with no news seen to boost prices either way.
"There is no strength in the market," said Vinod Kumar, director of Singapore metal company Donald Mcarthy.
"I think the mood in the market will continue to remain bearish," another dealer said.

Traders said there was no immediate impact on the market from news that some 300 workers at the giant Escondida copper mine in northern Chile have voted to strike although they were keeping a close watch on developments.
Three-month copper was quoted by the trade at 0200 GMT at $2,275/80 a tonne, slightly easier from the close in London on Tuesday of $2,281.
Three-month aluminium was seen by regional dealers at 0200 GMT at $1,553/58 a tonne against the close in London of $1,555.
Base metal demand around the region remained steady, "but not spectacular," a dealer said.
There were some spot deals done by Chinese buyers although the levels were not all that heavy, traders said.

LME copper stocks are seen continuing their recent falls and will probably slip by between 1,000-3,000 tonnes when the LME's daily report is released at 0800 GMT, dealers said. Aluminium stocks are also tipped to decline by 1,000-3,000 tonnes.
The volume of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse may slip later on Wednesday. Inventories reached 28,525 tonnes in the LME stocks report on Tuesday, down 375 tonnes from last Monday's report.
